sources.text:
Podyjí National Park (Czech: Národní park Podyjí) is a national park in the South Moravian Region of the Czech Republic. Adjacent to Austria's Thayatal National Park on the border, together they are referred to as the Inter-National park. Podyjí is one of the Czech Republic's four national parks. It protects near-natural forests along the deep Dyje River valley. The well-preserved state of the biome of the park is cited as being unique in Central Europe.


== Legal status ==
Podyjí National Park is one of the four national parks of the Czech Republic. It has an area of 63 square kilometres (24 sq mi) and buffer zone of 29 square kilometres (11 sq mi). It was formally declared a national park on 1 July 1991 by government order no. 164/1991. BirdLife International (IBA) has included this park under its criteria C6, covering a larger area of 76.66 square kilometres (29.60 sq mi). In February 2025, a new director, Pavel Müller, will take up his duties.
On February 1, 2026, environmentalist, and longtime director of the park, Tomáš Rothröckl died.
